frase_gancho.texto: A courtyard where construction tools appeared.

puente_narrativo.texto: Follow your route: continue through the spaces of work and power in the city.

guion_corto.texto: This building is called the Temple of the Architects, also the Sunken Courtyard. According to the INAH guide, construction tools appeared there: plumb bobs, mixers and polishers. A plumb bob is a string with a weight used to check that a wall is vertical. A polisher smooths the surface of stone. INAH Lugares describes in the eastern complex a rectangular building with a sunken courtyard, which may be this very one. Modern names say more about those who gave them than about those who built. Even so, seeing building tools here is a reminder that someone had to measure, level and polish every stone. It is a good place to think about trades.

guion_largo.texto:
The name sounds like a title, but it comes from what was found here.

It is called the Temple of the Architects, and also the Sunken Courtyard. According to the INAH guide, construction tools appeared in this place: plumb bobs, mixers and polishers.

A plumb bob is a string with a weight at the tip. It serves to check that a wall is straight. A polisher is a stone used to smooth the surface of another.

INAH Lugares mentions, in the eastern complex, a rectangular building with a sunken courtyard. It may be the same one.

Modern names say more about those who gave them than about those who built. Nobody knows what this building was called in the city. What we do know is what the find suggests: tools for construction work were kept or used here.

Think about the work behind a city like this. Someone had to measure, level, cut and polish every stone, and lay out terraces on a hill.

When you look at the sunken courtyard, imagine those tools on the floor. It is a way of seeing the builders, and not only the rulers.

texto.Names: Temple of the Architects and Sunken Courtyard
texto.Find: plumb bobs, mixers and polishers, according to the INAH guide

texto.pregunta: Myth: A temple is always a place only for gods.
texto.respuesta: Reality: The modern name comes from the construction tools found, not from a proven religious function.
